records.name: Usiloquy Dance Designs
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that teaches Bharatanatyam, a classical Indian dance, and makes and performs its own dance productions. It offers classes at three levels and workshops for children, families and adults.
records.what_you_do: Take an ongoing beginner, intermediate or advanced Kalakshetra-style Bharatanatyam class, book a workshop, or see a free public performance the group lists on its events page.

schedule.text: Ongoing Kalakshetra-style Bharatanatyam classes at beginner, intermediate and advanced levels. Class days and times are not published, so ask for the current schedule.

cost.text: Class fees and workshop prices are not published on the group's pages. Ask when you get in touch.

first_step.how: Email shaily@usiloquydance.org or call 267-324-5917 to ask about the next beginner class and the current class times. You can also book a workshop with the workshop booking button on the repertoire page.
first_step.basis: Beginner classes are offered, and the site gives an email, a phone number and a contact page to ask. Class times and a trial class are not published, so you need to ask before you plan a first visit.
first_step.what_to_expect: Classes use the Kalakshetra style and run at beginner, intermediate and advanced levels. The site does not say how long a class lasts, what it costs, or whether a trial class is offered. Workshops are another way in: an introduction for children ages 7 to 12, a technique session for adults, and a family workshop for mixed ages.
first_visit_tips: Ask for the studio address and class times, since neither is published.
Ask whether a trial class is offered before you sign up.
Watch the events page for free public performances, which are listed by date.

records.notes: The batch id ends in -copy. It is the only Usiloquy file in data/groups, so no duplicate was found. Classes are confirmed on the home page, but days, times, fees and trial classes are not published on any page read. The events page lists one upcoming free event, a performance at a library in Westampton, New Jersey on Nov 1, 2026. That is outside Philadelphia and was not used. The sign of life is the tier 1 Fall Arts Fest listing.

records.name: VC Philadelphia
records.summary: The Philadelphia chapter of the Video Consortium, a network for nonfiction filmmakers. Each month it holds an in person gathering, such as a screening, panel, workshop or social evening.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly gathering to meet other nonfiction filmmakers and hear about jobs and resources. Members also get a jobs board, a directory profile and a weekly newsletter.

schedule.text: Monthly in person gatherings around Philadelphia, with screenings, panels, workshops and social evenings. Dated listings are on the events page.

locations.label: The Philadelphia Inquirer, Suite 600 (venue for a listed gathering)

cost.text: Essential membership is free with a one time $10 application fee. Gold membership is $119 a year or $12.50 a month, and an annual Gold plan waives the application fee. Gold members attend gatherings free. The site does not give a price for other attendees. Students get half off the fees.

first_step.how: Email philadelphia@videoconsortium.org to ask whether a non-member can come to a gathering. If you work or study in nonfiction video, you can also apply for an Essential membership at videoconsortium.org/join. The $10 fee is one time, and reviews take about 2 to 5 business days.
first_step.basis: Joining needs an application that is reviewed before you become a member, and eligibility is limited to people who work or study in nonfiction video. The site does not say whether a non-member can attend a gathering.
first_step.what_to_expect: Gatherings are monthly, in person and social. A typical evening, as one listed gathering shows, starts with about an hour of mingling, then a short film screening, a talk with the filmmakers, a raffle, and time to network, with light refreshments. The site does not say how long a gathering lasts overall.
first_visit_tips: Bring ID, which the event listing asks for.
Check the events page for the date, time and venue before you go.
Apply well before a gathering, since reviews take about 2 to 5 business days.

records.notes: The venue shown is for the Oct 14, 2026 gathering, which is a Wednesday and matches the tier 1 Wednesday pattern. Other gatherings may use other venues. The events page says Gold members attend free but does not say what a non-member pays, so the cost text keeps what tier 1 had.

records.name: VETMOTO
records.summary: A nonprofit motorcycle shop where veterans and at-risk young people learn engine repair and trade skills, with basic skills classes in resume writing and leadership.
records.what_you_do: Members learn introductory trade skills and engine repair and take basic skills classes. Volunteers help with shop maintenance and facility projects at the VetMotoShop, and mentors support members.

schedule.text: Shop hours and class times are not published on the pages we could read. Ask the group which days volunteers are needed.

cost.text: The site lists no fee to take part. The group asks for donations.

first_step.how: Call (215) 586-3494 or use the contact form on vetmoto.org to ask about volunteering at the VetMotoShop, or visit the shop to help on a project.
first_step.basis: The site invites people to volunteer on shop projects and gives a phone number and a contact form. It describes no application for volunteers. Rules for who can take part as a member are not spelled out.
first_step.what_to_expect: The shop is a working space for motorcycle and engine repair, and volunteers help with maintenance and facility projects. The site does not describe a typical visit or how long a session runs, so ask the group before you come.
first_visit_tips: Call ahead, since shop hours are not listed online.
Ask what project needs help and what to wear for shop work.
Ask how to get to the shop, since the site does not describe parking or transit.

records.notes: The home page and the get-involved page name no eligibility rules, shop hours or class calendar. The only year on the home page is in the footer copyright, which is not evidence, so status stays probably_active with no dated sign of life. The phone and contact name come from the contact page, which tier 1 read, because the get-involved page lists neither.

records.name: Vetri Community Partnership Teaching Kitchen
records.summary: A nonprofit teaching kitchen on Spring Garden Street that runs public cooking classes and nutrition education for people of all ages.
records.what_you_do: Take part in a public cooking class, or ask about classes for a group. The group also rents its kitchen space to community and corporate groups.

schedule.text: Public classes are listed on the group's class calendar. Days, times and dates were not on the pages we could read.

cost.text: The pages we could read do not list a class price. Ask when you get in touch.

first_step.how: Call 215-600-2630 or email info@vetricommunity.org to ask for the next public class, its time, and how to sign up.
first_step.basis: The group says it welcomes people of all ages, and it lists a phone number and an email to ask. Class dates and sign-up steps are not on the pages we could read, so a person has to ask.
first_step.what_to_expect: Public classes are hands-on cooking sessions in the group's teaching kitchen on Spring Garden Street, open to people of all ages. The pages we could read do not give class length, price or sign-up steps, so ask before you plan a visit.
first_visit_tips: Ask for the next class date and start time before you plan a visit.
Ask what the class costs and whether you need to register ahead.

records.notes: vetricommunity.org returned HTTP 403 to the fetch tool on its home page, so its class calendar and news pages could not be read (see blocked). One web search returned a summary with a class schedule, a price and a suite number, drawn from pages that could not be read directly. Those details are not recorded here. A person should confirm dates, times and price on the class calendar before a visit. The map page lists no class days, prices or registration method, so the first step now points to a phone call rather than a class schedule link.

records.name: Vilna Congregation
records.summary: A congregation on Pine Street in Philadelphia led by Rabbi Menachem Schmidt. The website does not list service times or classes, so visitors contact the rabbi directly.
records.what_you_do: Contact Rabbi Schmidt to ask about services and learning, or support the congregation with an online donation.

schedule.text: The website does not list service times. Ask the rabbi.

cost.text: The site lists no dues and has an online donation form.

first_step.how: Email the rabbi at menschmidt@gmail.com or call (215) 435-0646 to ask about services and how to visit.
first_step.basis: The website asks visitors to contact the rabbi for service times. It describes no classes, membership steps or visitor programs, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The website does not describe a visit. Ask the rabbi which services are held, when they start, and whether a visitor is welcome at a service or a learning session.
first_visit_tips: Ask the rabbi for the service times and where to enter before you go.
Ask what to wear, since the site does not say.

records.notes: The site's links go back to its own home page, a donate section and an external ritual bath (mikvah) site. Dropped as a lead: Mikvah Mei Shalva (philamikvah.org), a ritual bath facility named on the site and not a community group for this directory, not fetched. The site's only year is a 2022 footer, which is not evidence, so status stays probably_active with no dated sign of life. The email is the one the site gives for asking about service times.

records.name: Virtual Grief Support Group: All Arms Locked
records.summary: Free online group for men grieving a loss that carries stigma, such as overdose, addiction, homicide or suicide. Philly HEALs runs it.
records.what_you_do: Meet other men with similar losses, build a circle of people who understand, and learn ways to cope with grief.

first_step.how: Fill in the Philly HEALs sign-up survey linked from the city's grief support page to get the meeting link. To ask questions, call Philly HEALs staff at (215) 982-0959.
first_step.basis: The group is open to men with this kind of loss, it is free, and the city page gives a clear sign-up route.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each session runs one hour, 6 to 7 pm Eastern on Mondays, online. It is for men grieving a loss that carries stigma, and you meet other men with similar losses. The page does not say which online platform is used, whether cameras are on, or who leads the session.
first_visit_tips: Sign up early so the meeting link reaches you before the session.
Choose a quiet, private spot with a good internet connection for the hour.
Ask Philly HEALs ahead of time which platform is used, since the page does not say.

records.notes: The city page does not name this group. The Healthy Minds Philly event page and its monthly listing do, with Philly HEALs as the organizer. The phone is one of the Philly HEALs staff lines the city page lists. Sign-up uses a city survey, which was not submitted. The city page also names six other Philly HEALs peer groups, listed in leads_only. The event page's other listings (a Grief and Loss Workshop on Oct 29, 2026 and a caregiver group on Nov 3, 2026) are separate events and were not recorded.

records.name: Visitation B.V.M. Parish
records.summary: A Catholic parish on Kensington Avenue with Sunday Masses in Spanish, English and Vietnamese, and a Saturday evening Mass in English.
records.what_you_do: Come to Mass in Spanish, English or Vietnamese. The parish also runs a religious education program for children and names an adult welcome and initiation program (R.C.I.A.) on its site.

schedule.text: Sunday Masses at 8 am (Spanish), 9:30 am (English), 10 am (Spanish, in the upper church) and 11 am (Vietnamese). Saturday vigil Mass at 5 pm in English. Weekday Mass Monday to Saturday at 8:30 am, and a Spanish Mass at 7 pm on Tuesday and Wednesday. Confession on Saturday from 4 to 5 pm.

cost.text: Attending Mass has no charge. The parish invites giving through its ParishGiving sign-up.

first_step.how: Come to any Mass on the schedule. To ask about joining as an adult, call the parish office at (215) 634-1133.
first_step.basis: Masses are open to anyone, and the parish lists a phone number and an email for questions. The parish pages do not describe a newcomer program for adults, so the adult program needs a phone call.
first_step.what_to_expect: Mass is offered in Spanish, English or Vietnamese, depending on the service you pick. The parish lists no sign-up for attending Mass. The parish pages do not say how long Mass lasts or what happens afterward, so ask the office if you want to know more.
first_visit_tips: Pick the language you want: Spanish at 8 and 10 am on Sunday, English at 9:30 am and Saturday at 5 pm, Vietnamese at 11 am.
Call the office at (215) 634-1133 for directions, since the parish pages give two addresses.
Confession is on Saturday from 4 to 5 pm, or by appointment, if you want it before Mass.

records.notes: Tier 1 gave the church as Lehigh Ave. and B St. (cross streets). The parish's own about and contact pages give 2646 Kensington Ave., and its sacraments page gives the rectory at 2625 B St. The record uses those addresses. The no charge statement for Mass is carried from tier 1; no page read today says it. The Community Center at Visitation is named on the parish site and is in leads_only. Dropped as leads: Visitation BVM School (a parish school, not a community group for this directory, not fetched) and the Redemptorists of the Baltimore Province (the religious order the clergy belong to, not fetched). The Oct 9, 2026 daily readings line is the dated sign of life. The adult R.C.I.A. program has a name on the about page but no details, so the first step is a phone call.
